verdict.rationale: Capacities documents a REST API, with an OpenAPI spec and a TypeScript SDK, that reads and writes objects, block content and daily notes. It also offers an official MCP integration and Chat Connectors that let external assistants such as Claude and Cursor change notes without the GUI. The OpenAPI probe's 404s on docs.capacities.io do not contradict this, because the spec is published at api.capacities.io. The Beta API is being replaced by a successor API rather than removed. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that agent read/write works in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent or assistant can read AND write my notes headlessly — through a documented local API, vendor API, or MCP server — without me touching the GUI

citations.quote: The Capacities REST API gives you programmatic access to a workspace space — read and write objects, properties, block content, daily notes, and more.
The Capacities API is a REST API that allows you access, create and manipulate your content.
Build your own app, agent, or bot and integrate it with a Capacities space by implementing a custom MCP client using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) open standard.
Chat Connectors let you connect AI chat apps, like ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, or Le Chat, to your Capacities space.
If an external assistant changes a note in a way you do not want, use Version history on that object to preview and restore an earlier version.
